title: Demo tenant: scope API keys to least privilege + rotation helpers + audit log coverage
author: Ethan Park
release_notes: - Demo tenant keys are now created with scoped permissions by default (project + route + operation). - Added rotation helper to generate/roll keys and verify audit-log entries. - Added audit log coverage for key create/rotate/revoke events (including actor + reason).
description: Context: SEs and AEs have been sharing a single broadly-permissioned demo API key for convenience. This has caused a few recurring problems: (1) unclear blast radius when a key leaks in a screen share/recording, (2) brittle access when RBAC mappings change (INT-993), (3) hard-to-debug 429s / quota overrides (SUP-4127) because traffic sources are indistinguishable, and (4) audit log gaps for key lifecycle events. This PR tightens demo-tenant API key scopes to least privilege, adds rotation helpers for the demo reset flow, and ensures we emit consistent audit-log events for key create/rotate/revoke. Summary of changes (single-tenant + parallel demos friendly): 1) New scoped key model for demo workflows: - Introduce explicit permission bundles for demo use cases: `demo.chat.invoke`, `demo.embeddings.invoke`, `demo.routes.read`, `demo.console.read`, `demo.eval.run` (internal), `demo.traffic.seed` (job-only). - Scope keys by (org_id, project_id) and optionally (route_id); default is project scope + specific route allowlist for the standard demo routes. - Disallow admin/control-plane mutations from demo keys by default (no model pin edits, no org role changes, no billing settings). - Add optional `--ttl` for short-lived keys (defaults to 24h for SE-run keys, 2h for externally shared “live demo” keys). 2) Rotation + safe sharing helpers: - Add `rw demo keys create` and `rw demo keys rotate` helpers used by the reset runbook. - Rotation is implemented as: create new key -> update demo app secret refs -> revoke old key (with a 10 minute overlap option). - Adds a `rw demo keys verify-audit` command that checks for expected audit log events over the last N minutes and prints pass/fail with reasons. - Adds guardrails to prevent generating demo keys outside the demo org (requires `DEMO_ORG_ID` match and `--i-know-what-im-doing` escape hatch for on-call). 3) Audit logging: - Emit audit events for `api_key.created`, `api_key.rotated`, `api_key.revoked` with consistent fields: actor_id, actor_type (user/service), org_id, project_id, key_id (opaque), scope_summary, ttl_seconds, reason, ip/user_agent (when applicable). - Ensure rotations emit both `created` (new key) and `revoked` (old key) with `rotation_id` correlation for easier demo incident review. - Add a small backfill shim in the audit pipeline for demo keys created via legacy endpoints (so we don’t regress reporting during rollout). 4) Migration/compatibility: - Existing demo keys continue to work but are marked as `legacy_unscoped=true` and will be refused by `rw demo reset` after 2025-12-15 (soft enforcement: warning now, hard error later). - The demo app (redwood-examples) is unchanged in this PR; it only relies on the hosted inference endpoints. However, the default demo-tenant bootstrap now provisions route-specific keys so the app doesn’t require broad project permissions. Why this approach: - We need demo keys to be shareable (screen share) but low-risk. Route allowlists plus short TTL makes accidental exposure less consequential. - Separating “seed traffic” permissions keeps the synthetic traffic generator from inheriting unnecessary inference permissions. - Audit log correlation makes it easy to answer security-review questions live (“show me key creation, who did it, and when”). Testing: - Unit tests for scope evaluation (project + route allowlist + operation) and TTL enforcement. - Integration test: create scoped key -> call chat completion on allowed route -> expect 200; call embeddings on disallowed route -> expect 403 with `scope_denied`. - Integration test: rotate key -> old key revoked -> verify audit events exist with same rotation_id. - Manual: Markus ran through the SE demo runbook on staging demo tenant; verified the console read-only key can view dashboards but cannot edit routes/models. Rollout plan: - Merge behind feature flag `demo_scoped_keys_default=true` for demo org only. - Enable in demo prod tenant after PR-28531 healthcheck rollout so SEs have a single pass/fail signal. - Communicate to GTM: new default keys are time-bound; reset tooling will automatically refresh them. Security considerations: - No customer data impacted (demo-only). - Avoid logging raw API key material anywhere (only key_id and scope summary). - Audit event payload intentionally excludes key prefixes. Follow-ups: - Add UI affordance in Console to show “scope summary” for a key (read-only) for SE demos (tracked in ENG-4855 subtask). - Update internal demo docs/runbook with the new commands (Elliot to pick up once merged).
commits: auth: add scoped permission bundles for demo keys
control-plane: enforce project/route allowlists in API key middleware
cli: add rw demo keys create/rotate/verify-audit
audit: emit api_key.* events with rotation correlation id
tests: add integration coverage for scoped keys and rotation
review_conversation: Naomi Feldman (Security): Can we confirm we never include the key prefix in audit logs? I’ve seen teams accidentally log first 6 chars for “debugging.”

Ethan Park (Author): Confirmed. Events include only key_id (UUID) + scope_summary. I added a test asserting we don’t serialize `api_key` fields into the audit payload, and I removed one debug log in the legacy endpoint that printed `token_hint`.
Marcus Lin (Security Eng): TTL defaults—24h for SE keys feels long for something that gets screenshared. Could we make “live demo” keys default to 2h and require an explicit flag for longer TTL?

Ethan Park (Author): Done. `rw demo keys create` defaults to 2h unless `--purpose se-run` is specified (24h). The reset command uses `--purpose se-run` so internal dry-runs don’t constantly rotate mid-demo. Added messaging in CLI output: “do not paste into chat / slides; use vault link.”
Sean Gallagher (SRE): Please ensure rotation is non-disruptive. Overlap window + rollback path?

Ethan Park (Author): Rotation helper supports `--overlap=10m` (default). It writes the new key first, validates healthcheck call, then revokes the old key. If validation fails, it leaves the old key active and prints a clear rollback message. I also wired `verify-audit` to fail soft (warning) so we don’t block demos if the audit pipeline is delayed.
Chloe Martin (Console): For `demo.console.read`, are we sure it doesn’t grant access to billing tabs / org settings? We’ve had accidental exposure during exec demos.

Ethan Park (Author): It’s scoped to Console resources under Project only (dashboards, traces, rollouts view) and explicitly denies org/billing endpoints. I added a regression test for `GET /org/settings` returning 403 when using a console-read key.
Markus Klein (Demo owner): Ran through the reset flow. Much better. One request: CLI output should print “where to paste” (env var name) and redact the token in logs by default.

Ethan Park (Author): Updated CLI: prints token once to stdout with a “copy now” banner; subsequent logs only reference key_id. Also added `--json` mode for automation that returns the token in a single line (no extra logging).
Naomi Feldman (Security): Approving contingent on a follow-up to document least-privilege rationale for sales enablement so SEs can answer ‘why do you need this permission?’ quickly.
Ethan Park (Author): Agree. I added a short section to tools/rw-cli/README.md and linked ENG-4855 for the full enablement doc update.
